newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgarian bank creditor jumps repayment queue. [CORRECTED 15:50 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian bank creditor jumps repayment queue. [CORRECTED 15:50 GMT]

text.p: A Liechtenstein-based creditor of Bulgaria's insolvent state-owned Mineralbank has jumped the repayment queue with a Swiss court ruling allowing it to receive $12 million from Mineralbank's accounts abroad, newspapers said on Monday.

"On September 24, a Swiss Court ruled on Mineralbank case in favour of the Liechtenstein-based Paton Anstalt, allowing the company to seize some $12 million from bank's blocked accounts," Banker weekly (Corrects source from Kapital newspaper) said.
Bulgarian businessman Georgi Naidenov, who represents Paton Anstalt and is a major shareholder in Bulgaria's private Teximbank, declined comment.
Banking officials said the seized sum might rise to around $13 million because it included interest payments.
Some $10 million are blocked in Swiss banks and another $3 million are frozen in Bulgarian banks.

"The situation is very complicated because the Bulgarian court has not ruled on Mineralbank's insolvency so far, which allowed Paton Anstalt to take a legal action to retrieve its dues ahead of other creditors," a Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) official said.
Last year Paton Anstalt purchased loans worth $19.9 million by Austria's Donau Bank to Mineralbank and tried to settle them at a 40 percent discount by an agreement with Mineralbank.
After Mineralbank failed to repay the debt to Naidenov's company, Paton Anstalt launched a lawsuit in Switzerland and blocked several Mineralbank accounts in Bulgarian and foreign banks.

In February the Bank Consolidation Company, which manages state equity in commercial banks and owns a majority stake in Mineralbank, restricted the powers of the bank's management in a bid to prevent them acting unfairly against other bank creditors.

Mineralbank's foreign debt amounts to $242 million, including a five billion yen issue of Samurai bonds, which the bank failed to service after it was put in receivership by the central bank in May due to a danger of insolvency.
On May 31 the BNB filed an insolvency suit against Mineralbank.
Under Bulgaria's banking law, creditors of a bank that is declared insolvent by the court can be paid only after the bank's liquidation through the courts.
The Sofia City Court has postponed ruling on Mineralbank insolvency several times since May and the next court session is set for November 27.
